About
School of Electrical and Mechanical Engineering
Building a more secure, sustainable society through world-class research and teaching
Adelaide University’s School of Electrical and Mechanical Engineering (EME) offers degrees, programs and disciplines in Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Biomedical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechatronic Engineering, Maritime Engineering, Engineering Management, and Aviation.
The Engineering expertise offered by EME sees our world-class researchers, alumni and students pioneer technologies, launch startups, and lead companies, driving local and global impact. Our Aviation programs equip the next generation of aviation professionals with expertise in aviation theory and its real-world applications in flight operations, management and safety, with knowledge in aerodynamics, meteorology, navigation, flight planning, and aircraft systems.
Discover the School of Electrical and Mechanical Engineering
Explore our study areas
Our study areas span Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering and Aviation. Our engineering programs include specialisations in Biomedical, Mechatronic, Maritime, Electrical Power and Aerospace engineering.
Explore our study areas
Discover our research
Our world-class scholars, alumni, and students push the boundaries of engineering and science – inventing new technologies, launching successful startups, managing technology companies – positively impacting society in South Australia, the nation, and beyond.

About the School of Electrical and Mechanical Engineering
From developing the key technologies driving our future prosperity and well-being, to flying aeroplanes, discover how our school is empowering the next generation of electrical, mechanical, biomedical, mechatronic, aerospace and maritime engineers and aviation professionals.
About us
Research capabilities
Our research leads groundbreaking multidisciplinary engineering research, advancing autonomous systems, biomedical and medical devices, space, defence, sustainability, energy systems, sensors, telecommunications, RF sensing, advanced materials, manufacturing, fluid mechanics, acoustics, semiconductors, photonics, and quantum technologies through global collaboration.
